headline: Split the list conceptually into an already reversed prefix and an untouched suffix
statement: Reverse all next pointers of a singly linked list and return its new head. An empty list returns an empty list.
intuition: Reverse one link at a time. Before changing a node's next link, save where it originally led. Point the current node back to the reversed part, then continue from the saved next node. Saving that link is what keeps the rest of the list reachable.
approach: Save current.next as following before modifying it.
Set current.next=previous, advance previous to current, and current to following.
Return previous after the original suffix is empty.
correctness: The reversed prefix initially is empty. Each iteration links the first untouched node in front of that prefix while preserving every untouched node through following. Thus all processed links are reversed with no lost nodes; when current is None, previous is the complete reversed list.
bruteForce: Store all node references, then reconnect them in reverse: O(n) additional space.

complexity.explanation: Each original node is transferred once from the untouched suffix to the reversed prefix. Only previous, current, and following pointers are needed; no output nodes are allocated.

pitfalls: Saving following after overwriting current.next loses the suffix.
Return previous, since current is None at the end.
Reverse links rather than copying reversed values into nodes.
